title: the hollow reads a tooth this host cannot run as unread, not as red at HEAD
intention: cairn test --hollow on a host that cannot run some of a proof's declared teeth reads those teeth as unread on this host, not as red at HEAD, measures the reversion with the teeth that did run, and names the unread teeth in the seal beside the reading.
why: Measured 2026-11-23: two tickets hold at PROVEME on it. On Linux, 8c829d9b38b8's hollow raised HollowUnmeasurable at the HEAD baseline: test_on_windows_a_pulse_owns_no_python_exe_no_conhost_and_no_visible_console printed UNRAN, so the tester named it in not_run_teeth and wrote no red (device.py:969, ticket 64ae0df3f1f3). The hollow's baseline still computes missing = declared - teeth_green, so that tooth read as 'not green at HEAD' and teeth 2 and 3 never measured the heartbeat.py revert. 364704f371dd's Linux hollow refused the same way on its off-NT Unmeasured tooth. Both proofs are sealed green on Windows on these exact bytes. The information is already in the record the baseline reads, and it is dropped one line later.
traces_to: Law 3 (a tooth this host did not run measured nothing; reading it as red is an unmeasured claim), Law 7 (a diagnostic may not collapse 'not run here' into 'failed'), Law 8 (the teeth that ran still have to red on the revert).
how: In hollow.py's run_all, keep each proof's record['evidence'].get('not_run_teeth') per proof. In the baseline, subtract those teeth from both the missing set and the declared set every later reading watches. Write evidence['hollow_not_run'][tid] = {proof_rel: sorted(teeth)} beside evidence['hollow'] through the seal write already in use, never inside evidence['hollow'][tid], because clearance.hollow_lacks reads any non-list value there as unreadable. When every declared tooth of a proof is not run on this host, raise HollowUnmeasurable naming the proof, the teeth and 'not run on this host'. A tooth that ran and failed at HEAD refuses exactly as today. Clearance does not change.

clauses.claim: a scratch proof whose tooth A reads the subject and whose tooth B prints UNRAN on this host: reverting the subject reds A, and the hollow returns the reading {subject: [A]} with B named under hollow_not_run, raising no HollowUnmeasurable
the same fixture with tooth A not reading the subject: the reading is {subject: []}, so PROVED's hollow_file rule still reds it
a scratch proof whose declared teeth all print UNRAN on this host: HollowUnmeasurable is raised and its message names those teeth as not run on this host
a scratch proof whose tooth B ran and failed at HEAD (a real red, no UNRAN): HollowUnmeasurable is raised as before, naming B as not green at HEAD

decisions.text: D1: hollow.py's run_all keeps not_run_teeth per proof; the baseline subtracts them from missing and from the declared teeth later readings watch; the all-UNRAN case raises HollowUnmeasurable naming the host.
D2: the unread teeth are written as evidence['hollow_not_run'][tid] = {proof_rel: [teeth]}, beside evidence['hollow'], never inside the per-file reading clearance.hollow_lacks reads.
D3: a new proof drives the hollow over scratch repos, one tooth per clause; its UNRAN tooth prints the line device.py's unran_only parses, the way ground_loop's host-bound proof does.

out: a Windows-side hollow of a proof born in its build commit (unmeasured here)

measured.saw: 8c829d9b38b8 Linux hollow: HollowUnmeasurable, teeth_not_green [test_on_windows_a_pulse_owns_no_python_exe_no_conhost_and_no_visible_console], of_declared 3, teeth_that_ran_at_all 3; the tester printed 'NOT SEALED — every failing tooth was not run on this host'
364704f371dd Linux hollow refused 'no reversion reading can be attributed' on its off-NT Unmeasured tooth
hollow.py's baseline computes missing = declared_teeth - teeth_green and never reads evidence.not_run_teeth, which device.py:839-842 sets
